newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU urged to adapt schools to Internet era.
newsitem.headline: EU urged to adapt schools to Internet era.

text.p: The European Union must act urgently to adapt its schools to the Internet era or risk U.S. domination of educational materials, the European Commission said on Wednesday.
"We must be aware that European schools lag far behind compared with what is going on elsewhere," Research and Education Commissioner Edith Cresson told a news conference.
The Commission, the EU executive, proposed an action plan that aims to boost the use of computers, CD-ROMS and the Internet in the classroom.
It said it would channel existing EU funds to the task and called on private industry to join with public authorities to find ways to finance equipment, services and software.

"Any delay would make Europe increasingly dependent on non-European sources of educational and cultural material, since this is a market in which U.S. products currently predominate," it said in a statement.
"This would be a bitter blow for the cultural identity and linguistic diversity of the European Union."

Cresson said the EU could provide about 100 million Ecus ($125 million) over two years from its existing research, educational and technical programmes to help boost computer literacy in schools and produce more multimedia products.

The Commission, noting that fewer than five percent of European schools are hooked up to the Internet or other computer networks, said the plan should promote an EU-wide web of electronic educational networks.
The plan, which will go to EU ministers for approval, should stimulate development of multimedia teaching products, promote teacher training and sponsor publicity campaigns, it said.
